caps: Can a brain model that predicts fMRI almost perfectly be run backwards,
to read meaning out of the brain?
Project SBT_SW15 tests this on Meta's TRIBE v2.
Encoding models predict brain activity from what a person hears and sees.
Decoding is assumed to follow,
but for a deep foundation encoder, this has never been tested.
The frozen network, 177 million parameters,
is re-entered after feature aggregation,
and the stimulus is recovered by gradient descent,
against the known ground truth.
In the working model, the prediction error falls more than 300,000-fold.
Yet recovery stalls,
and equally good fits from different starts disagree.
On the real model, the brain-wide fit reaches an R² of 0.99,
while recovery stops near one half.
Across four ground truths, error falls 28-fold while recovery saturates.
Between equal solutions, the error rises almost 5-fold:
the inverse is non-convex.
The most responsive network, visual cortex, is the hardest to decode from.
On real fMRI, 4 of 5 story segments are identified amongst 45,
yet reconstruction reaches a cosine of only 0.02.
Encoding accuracy does not certify decoding.
Recoverability has to be measured.
